raw.assessment: Among 72 returned slips, 49 reported ten useful speaking minutes and 48 identified the intended preparation task. These do not establish rates across all 97 attendances. Coordination sometimes exceeded 90 minutes. Pairing delays, conversation-entry difficulty and task confusion suggest testable changes, but their causes remain unverified.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: quick provisional pairing followed by a shared fresh-start prompt and alternating speaking turns increases useful practice. Each prompt offers optional vocabulary support and an extension question; anyone can change partners without declaring a proficiency label.
openings.delta: Replace prolonged partner selection and assumed shared conversational history with immediate, reversible pairing and an entry point requiring no prior attendance, while retaining the familiar session sequence.
openings.prediction: Pair formation becomes shorter, occasional attendees report easier entry, and the lower-speaking partner receives more speaking time. Faster pairing without improved usefulness would weaken the proposed benefit.
openings.probe: Compare incumbent and modified sessions over six Wednesdays. Use anonymous observation to record pairing duration and speaking minutes for sampled pairs; collect usefulness reports from all attendees, including an optional prior-attendance item. Count missing reports separately and retain the ten-minute usefulness threshold.
assumptions: Optional supports offer sufficient challenge across participants' current levels.
Observation can occur within existing volunteer capacity; include its burden in weekly coordination totals.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: one reusable paper calendar containing six dated, standalone preparation tasks reduces confusion between earlier and upcoming tasks and lowers repeated messaging and printing effort.
openings.delta: Index preparation by explicit session date rather than relying on remembered attendance sequence. Distribute the calendar at every session, retain copies for newcomers and provide a brief arrival preparation opportunity when someone lacks the sheet.
openings.prediction: Earlier-task answers decrease, including among printed-information users, and information-handling time falls. Unchanged total coordination despite reduced messaging would indicate another activity dominates.
openings.probe: For six sessions, ask every attendee anonymously to identify the next dated preparation task; record missing answers and information channel. Volunteers log minutes by coordination activity, including calendar setup and printing. Assess the original 85% preparation and below-90-minute targets alongside speaking usefulness.
assumptions: Six conversational topics can be selected in advance without sacrificing usefulness.
Arrival preparation fits within 75 minutes and leaves adequate speaking time.
